events.title: Samsung Galaxy Note 8 released
events.summary: Samsung released the Samsung Galaxy Note 8 — dual cameras and S Pen after the Note 7 recall recovery.
events.about: The Galaxy Note targeted stylus power users on [Android]. Dual cameras and s pen after the note 7 recall recovery. Note apps and split-screen [Android] development often targeted this hardware class.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy Note 8 advanced Samsung's stylus phablet line.
narrative.whyImportant: Galaxy Note hardware defined large-screen [Android] productivity for years.
narrative.problemSolved: [Android] lacked a premium large-screen stylus flagship for note-taking workflows.

events.title: Safari 11 released
events.summary: Apple released Safari 11 on September 19, 2017 with macOS High Sierra — adding Intelligent Tracking Prevention, autoplay blocking, and [WebRTC] improvements.
events.about: Safari 11's Intelligent Tracking Prevention (ITP) limited cross-site cookies — reshaping ad tech and analytics. Autoplay blocking and reader mode refinements kept Safari focused on privacy and battery life as Chrome grew on desktop.

narrative.whyChosen: Safari 11's ITP was a watershed moment for web privacy and ad tracking.
narrative.whyImportant: Browser-level tracking prevention forced the ad industry to adapt measurement strategies.
narrative.problemSolved: Third-party cookies enabled pervasive cross-site tracking without user awareness.

events.title: iPhone 8 released
events.summary: Apple began selling the iPhone 8 on September 22, 2017 — adding wireless charging and the A11 Bionic chip in a familiar design.
events.about: The iPhone 8 refined the classic home-button iPhone while Apple bet the design future on iPhone X. Developers still targeted iPhone 8 class hardware as the conservative baseline through 2018.

narrative.whyChosen: The iPhone 8 was the last iteration of the classic Touch ID iPhone form.
narrative.whyImportant: Wireless charging and A11 performance kept a familiar target for [iOS] developers during the X transition.
narrative.problemSolved: Users wanted wireless charging without giving up the established home-button UX.

events.title: Equifax discloses massive data breach
events.summary: Equifax announced on September 7, 2017 that attackers had stolen personal data on 147 million Americans — names, Social Security numbers, and birth dates — via an unpatched Apache Struts flaw.
events.about: The breach exposed credit-bureau data that cannot be rotated like passwords — fueling identity-theft monitoring services and [GDPR]-style breach-notification debates in the U.S. Developers learned that unpatched Java web frameworks on internet-facing apps could leak half the country's PII; Equifax's CISO and CEO resigned amid congressional hearings.

narrative.whyChosen: Equifax was the breach that put 147 million SSNs on the dark web.
narrative.whyImportant: It made framework patching and breach disclosure timelines board-level issues.
narrative.problemSolved: Nothing for consumers — attackers exploited a known Struts CVE Equifax had failed to patch.
